overview: The Traditional Knowledge Digital Library (TKDL) is a collaborative initiative between the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR), Ministry of Science and Technology, and the Department of Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India. It aims to prevent the misappropriation of India's traditional knowledge by providing access to patent examiners at international patent offices. The database contains transcribed and digitized traditional knowledge from ancient Indian texts in five international languages (English, French, German, Spanish, Japanese) to facilitate prior art searches.
objectives: Prevent the grant of erroneous patents on India's traditional knowledge
Provide access to traditional knowledge in patent application languages to international patent offices
Digitize and transcribe traditional knowledge from ancient Indian texts
Facilitate prior art search for patent examiners worldwide
Protect India's traditional knowledge from biopiracy
Promote awareness and documentation of traditional knowledge systems
eligibility: TKDL is not a beneficiary-oriented scheme; it is a defensive database accessible to patent examiners under international agreements. Access is granted to patent offices that have signed access agreements with TKDL, including the European Patent Office (EPO), United States Patent and Trademark Office (USPTO), Japan Patent Office (JPO), United Kingdom Intellectual Property Office (UKIPO), and Canadian Intellectual Property Office (CIPO).
benefits: Prevents erroneous patent grants on traditional knowledge, provides prior art evidence to patent examiners, supports legal opposition and revocation of patents, enhances global awareness of India's traditional knowledge, and safeguards indigenous rights without financial compensation to individuals.
financial_support: TKDL does not provide direct financial support to individuals or entities. It is a knowledge repository initiative funded by the Government of India through CSIR and AYUSH for development, maintenance, and access management.
application_process: 1. Patent offices interested in accessing TKDL must negotiate and sign an access agreement with the TKDL Unit. 2. Upon agreement, access credentials are provided to authorized patent examiners. 3. Authorized users can search the TKDL database through the secure access portal. 4. Search results are used to assess novelty and inventive step in patent applications related to traditional knowledge.
deadlines: Rolling basis — access is granted upon execution of formal access agreements.
implementing_agency: Council of Scientific and Industrial Research (CSIR) and Department of Ayurveda, Yoga & Naturopathy, Unani, Siddha and Homoeopathy (AYUSH), Ministry of Health and Family Welfare
caveats: Access is restricted to patent offices that have signed formal access agreements
TKDL does not provide financial benefits or direct support to individuals or communities
The database is not publicly accessible; access is limited to authorized patent examiners
TKDL functions as a prior art repository and does not grant intellectual property rights
